terms.meaning: a project value already stored in the Yard with an active, linked source
a built-in tool that runs checks and reports which pass or fail

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File imports
sections.what: Imports the test tools, the hashing tool, the held-field functions and the collection function under test.
sections.why: Likely reason: the tests need these functions to check held-field behaviour.

sections.name: ev (part 1)
sections.title: Test helper and source and conflict checks
sections.what: Builds a sample Yard evidence row, then checks that a held field needs a value and a cited source, that cited budget and date disclosures count and replace forecasts, that conflicting values are not picked, and that quote checks for role work. Each check is a separate test.
sections.why: The test names state the rule: the module must not guess between conflicting figures and must not treat unsourced values as held.
sections.watch_out: The helper gives every sample row a default web address, so a test that needs an unsourced row must pass an empty address on purpose.

sections.name: ev (part 2)
sections.title: Collection skip and forecast tests
sections.what: Checks that the collection step does not ask the model about fields the Yard already holds, and makes no model call when every field is held. It also checks that forecast estimates are read from their own paths and must be worded as current estimates.
sections.why: The test names describe the intent: avoid researching fields the Yard already holds, and keep forecasts apart from final costs.
sections.watch_out: Some assertions look for quoted field names inside the prompt text, so renaming a field can make a check fail for the wrong reason.

summary: Test file for the logic that works out which project fields the Yard already holds. Only its import lines are in this packet, so its tests are not described.
purpose: Likely purpose: checks that held-field rules work without running a full scan.

how: Imports the held-field functions, the hashing tool and the collection function. The tests themselves are not in this packet.
risks: Coverage cannot be judged from the imports alone.
debug: Open the full file to read the tests, then run them with the built-in test runner.
